title: The finite fibre component has a clopen image in the integral closure
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a finite-type map of commutative rings, let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and write $B/IB=C_1\times C_2$ with $C_1$ finite over $A/I$. Let $B'\subseteq B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $B$, let $\phi:\operatorname{Spec}(B)\to\operatorname{Spec}(B')$ be induced by this inclusion, and let $T=\operatorname{Spec}(C_1)$, using the affine-spectrum convention [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Suppose $U\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}(B')$ is open, $T\subseteq\phi^{-1}(U)$, and the induced morphism $\phi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism of locally ringed spaces (a homeomorphism inducing isomorphisms on all local rings). Then $\phi(T)$ is open and closed in $\operatorname{Spec}(B'/IB')$, its inverse image under $\phi$ is exactly $T$, and the resulting product decomposition $B'/IB'=C'_1\times C'_2$ has $C'_1\to C_1$ an isomorphism and maps $C'_1$ into $C_1$ and $C'_2$ into $C_2$. The uses of the integral-closure inclusion and of clopen subsets of an affine spectrum are respectively [lem-weil-pbc-spec-integral-ring-map-integral] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent].
